question.text: Himalaya Mutual Fund wants to launch a 'Specialized Investment Fund' (SIF) — the new product line introduced by SEBI's amendment to the MF Regulations in December 2024. According to Section 2.4.2.4 of Chapter 2, what is the MINIMUM required investment amount from an investor in an SIF?

answer.text: Rs. 1 lakh across all investment strategies
Rs. 5 lakh across all investment strategies
Rs. 10 lakh across all investment strategies
Rs. 1 crore across all investment strategies

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 2.4.2.4 explicitly states that SIFs are 'sophisticated mutual funds where the minimum required investment amount is Rs. 10 lakhs from the investors across all investment strategies.' This was introduced vide SEBI (Mutual Funds) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2024 w.e.f. December 16, 2024. The Trap: Option A (1 lakh) conflates with PMS entry points. Option B (5 lakh) is a false intermediate. Option D (1 crore) is the AIF minimum — a classic Cat III vs SIF swap. SIF is an MF-based sophisticated structure at 10 lakh, NOT an AIF at 1 crore. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B (AIF Distributors) use INR 1 cr as the AIF minimum. XXI-A (PMS Distributor) uses INR 50 lakh for PMS. XIX-E must distinguish these thresholds precisely when explaining why an investor routes to a Cat III AIF rather than an SIF or PMS. Manager's Pro-Tip: SIFs are pitched as a 'Cat III-lite' mutual-fund wrapper — but they do NOT permit the same leverage, short-selling breadth, or performance-fee economics as a Cat III AIF. When a CIO asks 'why AIF not SIF', the answer is strategy breadth + leverage + HWM performance fee — not minimum ticket.
